gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many sunny days each kit's own panels need to refill it: the $3,199 2200X kit with one 200 W panel needs at least 2.5 days of continental-US sun (2,240 Wh ÷ 200 W ÷ 4.5 peak-sun h), while BLUETTI's $1,499 Elite 200 V2 kit with two 200 W panels needs about 1.2 days (2,073.6 Wh ÷ 400 W ÷ 4.5 h).
standout_why: I read powerstationgearlab.com's Patriot review (cited in 5 of 7 chats) and powerstations.reviews/4patriots-solar-generator. powerstationgearlab repeats 4Patriots' claim of '12-14 hours to recharge the 2200X from one 200W panel' and notes that the maximum solar input isn't published. It doesn't turn those hours into days of sun, and it gives no panel refill time for any rival kit. powerstations.reviews has $/Wh and weight for every model, but it says nothing about how long the bundled panel takes to recharge. ChatGPT's own answers only say the 200 W panel 'may take well over a day'. Both rival pages already have $/Wh, and Wh/lb follows directly from their stated Wh and weight, so neither number is new. solargenadvisor.com wouldn't load (SSL certificate error), so I couldn't check it.
decides: This supports BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the pick and points the page to a different bundle: the Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit at $1,499. It costs less than half the 2200X kit's $3,199 and has twice the panel wattage, so it refills in about 1 sunny day instead of 2.5 or more. It also accepts up to 1,000 W of solar. 4Patriots publishes no maximum solar input for the 2200X, so a buyer can't plan to add panels to shorten its refill. The two units weigh about the same per Wh, so weight doesn't separate them.

findings.label: Sunny days to refill from the kit's own panel (best case)
findings.value: 2.5 days at 4.5 peak-sun h/day; 2.8 days at 4.0
findings.source_title: Sun hours US map – Unbound Solar (NREL PVWatts/NSRDB data)
findings.note: 2,240 Wh ÷ 200 W = 11.2 panel-rated hours ÷ 4.5 PSH/day = 2.5 days. This assumes the panel delivers its full rated output with no charging losses, so real refills take longer. Unbound Solar: 'Most of the continental U.S. averages about 4 to 4.5 peak sun hours per day'; 'winter daily solar gain can run 25–50% below the yearly figure.'

findings.label: Maker's solar recharge claim compared with the physics
findings.value: 12–14 h claimed; the floor is 11.2 h at the panel's full 200 W
findings.source_title: Patriot Solar Generator Review (2026): Is 4Patriots Worth 3x the Price? – PowerStationGearLab
findings.note: Page: '4Patriots quotes 12-14 hours to recharge the 2200X from one 200W panel' and the maker 'doesn't publish a maximum solar input'. 2,240 ÷ 200 = 11.2 h, so the claim assumes 80–93% of rated output for 12–14 hours in a row. At 4–4.5 peak-sun h/day that is about 3 days of sun, not one.
